points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 1881年10月25日，毕加索出生于西班牙马拉加，父亲何塞·鲁伊斯·布拉斯科是当地美术学校的教授和画家。毕加索从小就展现出非凡的艺术天赋，据说在学会说话前就会画画。7岁时开始接受父亲的正规绘画训练，擅长写实风格。1891年，全家迁居拉科鲁尼亚，毕加索继续在父亲指导下学习绘画，并开始创作早期作品，如《科学与慈善》。这段时期奠定了他的绘画基础，并培养了他对艺术的早期热情。
points.descriptionEn: Born on October 25, 1881, in Málaga, Spain, Pablo Picasso was the son of José Ruiz Blasco, a painter and art professor. Picasso showed extraordinary artistic talent from a young age, reportedly drawing before he could speak. At age 7, he began formal art training under his father's guidance, mastering realistic styles. In 1891, the family moved to A Coruña, where Picasso continued his studies and created early works like 'Science and Charity.' This period laid the foundation for his artistic career and nurtured his early passion for painting.

points.title: 求学探索
points.description: 1897年，16岁的毕加索进入马德里圣费尔南多皇家美术学院学习。然而，他对学院保守的教学方法感到失望，经常逃课到普拉多博物馆临摹委拉斯开兹、戈雅等大师的作品。这段时期他深受西班牙传统绘画影响，同时开始接触现代艺术思潮。1899年，他回到巴塞罗那，加入了当地的前卫艺术圈，与艺术家们交流思想，探索新的艺术表达方式。这一阶段标志着他从传统学院派向现代艺术的转变。
points.descriptionEn: In 1897, at age 16, Picasso entered the Royal Academy of San Fernando in Madrid. However, he became disillusioned with the academy's conservative teaching methods and frequently skipped classes to copy works by masters like Velázquez and Goya at the Prado Museum. During this period, he was deeply influenced by Spanish traditional painting while also encountering modern artistic ideas. In 1899, he returned to Barcelona, joining the local avant-garde art circle and exchanging ideas with other artists, exploring new forms of artistic expression. This phase marked his transition from academic tradition to modern art.

points.title: 蓝色时期
points.description: 1901年至1904年间，毕加索在巴塞罗那和巴黎之间往返，创作了著名的'蓝色时期'作品。这一时期，他的画作以蓝色为主调，描绘贫困、孤独和绝望的主题，如《老吉他手》和《生命》。1902年，好友卡洛斯·卡萨吉马斯自杀，对毕加索产生深远影响，使他更加关注社会边缘人物的生活状态。在巴塞罗那，他与当地艺术家群体密切交往，参与前卫艺术活动，同时经济状况拮据，这也反映在他作品中对贫困主题的关注。蓝色时期标志着毕加索艺术风格的成熟，展现了他对社会现实的深刻关注。
points.descriptionEn: Between 1901 and 1904, Picasso traveled between Barcelona and Paris, creating his famous 'Blue Period' works. During this time, his paintings were dominated by blue tones, depicting themes of poverty, loneliness, and despair, such as 'The Old Guitarist' and 'La Vie.' In 1902, the suicide of his friend Carlos Casagemas deeply affected Picasso, leading him to focus more on the lives of social outcasts. In Barcelona, he closely associated with local artist groups and participated in avant-garde activities while facing financial difficulties, which is reflected in his focus on poverty themes. The Blue Period marked the maturation of Picasso's artistic style, demonstrating his deep concern for social reality.

points.title: 玫瑰时期
points.description: 1904年，毕加索定居巴黎，蒙马特区的'洗衣船'成为他的创作基地。这一时期，他的色彩从蓝色转向温暖的粉红色，主题也从贫困转向马戏团、杂耍艺人等较为轻松的题材，如《杂技演员的家庭》和《穿衬衫的女子'。1907年，毕加索创作了里程碑式的作品《亚威农少女》，开创了立体主义风格，彻底改变了现代艺术的发展方向。在巴黎，他与诗人阿波利奈尔、艺术家乔治·布拉克等人密切合作，共同探索艺术创新。这一时期是毕加索艺术生涯的关键转折点，他从传统绘画走向革命性的立体主义，奠定了他在现代艺术史上的重要地位。
points.descriptionEn: In 1904, Picasso settled in Paris, with the 'Bateau-Lavoir' in Montmartre becoming his creative base. During this period, his color palette shifted from blue to warmer pinks, and his themes moved from poverty to lighter subjects like circus performers and acrobats, as seen in 'Family of Saltimbanques' and 'Woman in a Shirt.' In 1907, Picasso created the groundbreaking work 'Les Demoiselles d'Avignon,' pioneering Cubism and fundamentally changing the course of modern art. In Paris, he collaborated closely with poets like Apollinaire and artists like Georges Braque, exploring artistic innovation. This period was a crucial turning point in Picasso's career, as he transitioned from traditional painting to revolutionary Cubism, establishing his significant place in art history.

points.title: 立体主义发展
points.description: 1909年至1919年间，毕加索与乔治·布拉克共同发展了立体主义艺术运动，将其分为'分析立体主义'和'综合立体主义'两个阶段。这一时期，他们打破了传统透视法，从多个角度同时呈现物体，如《小提琴与调色板》和《吉他》。1914年第一次世界大战爆发后，布拉克参军，毕加索留在巴黎，继续探索立体主义的同时，开始尝试新古典主义风格。1917年，他前往罗马为俄罗斯芭蕾舞团设计布景和服装，接触到了古典艺术和意大利文艺复兴艺术，这对他的创作产生了深远影响。这一时期，毕加索的立体主义风格日益成熟，成为20世纪最具革命性的艺术运动之一。
points.descriptionEn: Between 1909 and 1919, Picasso, together with Georges Braque, developed the Cubist art movement, dividing it into 'Analytic Cubism' and 'Synthetic Cubism' phases. During this period, they broke with traditional perspective, presenting objects simultaneously from multiple viewpoints, as seen in 'Violin and Palette' and 'Guitar.' When World War I broke out in 1914, Braque enlisted while Picasso remained in Paris, continuing to explore Cubism while beginning to experiment with Neoclassical style. In 1917, he traveled to Rome to design sets and costumes for the Russian Ballet, encountering classical art and Italian Renaissance, which profoundly influenced his work. During this period, Picasso's Cubist style matured, becoming one of the most revolutionary art movements of the 20th century.

points.title: 晚年创作
points.description: 1936年西班牙内战爆发后，毕加索的政治立场更加鲜明，创作了反法西斯名作《格尔尼卡》。二战期间，他留在巴黎，尽管德国占领军禁止他参展，但他继续创作，并秘密加入法国共产党。战后，毕加索成为国际艺术界的标志性人物，获得无数荣誉，包括1947年威尼斯双年展奖。1944年，他与画家弗朗索瓦丝·吉洛相识，开始了新的感情生活，并有了两个孩子。1950年代后，他转向陶艺创作，在法国南部穆然小镇建立了工作室。晚年，毕加索仍然保持极高的创作热情，不断尝试新的艺术形式，直到1973年4月8日在穆然逝世，享年91岁。他的晚年作品风格多变，但始终保持创新精神。
points.descriptionEn: After the outbreak of the Spanish Civil War in 1936, Picasso's political stance became more pronounced, leading to his creation of the anti-fascist masterpiece 'Guernica.' During World War II, he remained in Paris, continuing to create despite the German occupation's prohibition on exhibitions, and secretly joined the French Communist Party. Post-war, Picasso became an iconic figure in the international art world, receiving numerous honors, including the Venice Biennale award in 1947. In 1944, he met painter Françoise Gilot, beginning a new relationship that produced two children. After the 1950s, he turned to ceramics, establishing a studio in Mougins, southern France. In his later years, Picasso maintained an extraordinary creative passion, constantly experimenting with new forms until his death on April 8, 1973, in Mougins at age 91. His late works showed varied styles but always retained his innovative spirit.

supporter.zh: 毕加索被誉为20世纪最伟大的艺术家之一，他彻底改变了现代艺术的进程。作为立体主义的创始人，他打破了传统绘画的束缚，开创了全新的视觉语言。毕加索一生创作了超过5万件作品，涵盖绘画、雕塑、版画、陶瓷等多个领域，展现了惊人的创作力和多样性。他对艺术形式的不断探索和创新精神，激励了后世无数艺术家。毕加索不仅是艺术大师，也是文化符号，他的名字已成为创造力与变革的同义词。
supporter.en: Picasso is hailed as one of the greatest artists of the 20th century, who fundamentally transformed the course of modern art. As the co-founder of Cubism, he broke free from traditional painting constraints, creating a completely new visual language. With over 50,000 works across painting, sculpture, printmaking, and ceramics, Picasso demonstrated extraordinary creative power and diversity. His constant exploration of artistic forms and innovative spirit have inspired countless artists across generations. Picasso is not only a master artist but also a cultural icon, his name becoming synonymous with creativity and transformation.

critic.zh: 批评者认为毕加索的艺术成就伴随着个人道德争议。他对待女性的态度备受批评，多次抛弃长期伴侣和子女，包括与情人弗朗索瓦丝·吉洛所生的两个孩子被他拒绝承认。此外，毕加索在西班牙内战期间的政治立场虽然反法西斯，但也被指责为机会主义。一些艺术评论家认为他的后期作品缺乏早期作品的创新性，更多是重复自我而非突破。还有人质疑他'立体主义'的原创性，认为布拉克的贡献被低估。这些批评反映了艺术天才与个人道德之间的复杂关系。
critic.en: Critics argue that Picasso's artistic achievements were accompanied by significant personal moral controversies. His treatment of women has been widely condemned, with him repeatedly abandoning long-term partners and children, including refusing to acknowledge the two children he had with Françoise Gilot. Additionally, while his anti-fascist stance during the Spanish Civil War is acknowledged, he has been accused of opportunism. Some art critics contend that his later works lacked the innovation of his earlier pieces, representing more self-replication than breakthrough. Others question the originality of 'Cubism,' suggesting that Braque's contributions were undervalued. These criticisms reflect the complex relationship between artistic genius and personal morality.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，毕加索被定义为现代艺术的革命者和文化偶像。他的作品不仅改变了艺术史进程，也成为20世纪西方文化的象征。毕加索的名字超越了艺术领域，成为创造力、叛逆和变革的代名词。他的个人生活与艺术创作同样引人关注，使他成为媒体和公众讨论的焦点。在当代艺术市场，毕加索的作品创下天价，反映了他在艺术史上的不可替代地位。然而，学术界也日益关注其作品背后的社会历史语境，以及他与政治、文化运动的复杂关系，使对他的评价更加全面和多元。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Picasso is defined as a revolutionary of modern art and a cultural icon. His works not only transformed the course of art history but also became symbols of 20th-century Western culture. Picasso's name transcends the art world, becoming synonymous with creativity, rebellion, and transformation. His personal life is as scrutinized as his artistic creations, making him a focal point for media and public discussion. In the contemporary art market, Picasso's works command record prices, reflecting his irreplaceable position in art history. However, academia has increasingly focused on the socio-historical contexts of his work and his complex relationships with politics and cultural movements, leading to more comprehensive and diverse evaluations of his legacy.

self.zh: 艺术是一种谎言，它让我们更接近真实。
self.en: Art is a lie that makes us realize truth.

others.zh: 毕加索是我们这个时代最伟大的画家，他不仅是一位艺术家，更是一位创造者，他重新定义了艺术的本质。
others.en: Picasso is the greatest painter of our time. He is not only an artist but a creator who redefined the very essence of art.
